facilitation.title: Facilitation questions
facilitation.intro: Questions that help participants make their own decisions.
questions: What are you trying to show?
Where does your eye go first?
What happens if you move closer or lower?
Should the movement be sharp or blurred?
Which version communicates your idea most clearly?
reminders: Avoid correcting every photograph. Encourage experimentation and comparison.
Use “favorite,” “most interesting,” or “strongest experiment” rather than “best photograph.”
Do not ask everyone to present to the full group after every mission. Use pairs or groups of three and rotate partners.

time_cues: You have about four minutes left.
One minute left — what haven’t you tried?
Please mark one or two photographs that you want to revisit later.

welcome.title: Welcome and camera setup
goals: Make an opening photograph before giving instruction.
checks: Batteries and memory cards are ready.
Everyone knows how to focus and take a photograph.
Participants understand the physical boundaries of the group.
welcome.opening_message: Today is about noticing, experimenting, and having fun. There are no wrong photographs during an experiment. We’ll try different ideas, compare the results, and choose the photographs that interest us most.
safety: Stop walking before looking through the camera.
Stay within the defined activity area.
Watch for traffic, cyclists, stairs, and other pedestrians.
Ask before photographing recognizable people closely.
Do not enter private property or block sidewalks and entrances.
welcome.assignment: Without thinking too much, make one photograph showing how the city feels right now.
welcome.assignment_note: Do not critique these images. They will become the beginning of each participant’s final collection.

theory.title: Fast photography fundamentals
theory.intro: Keep cameras in participants’ hands. Spend approximately two minutes on each concept.

closing.title: Return and closing photograph
closing.body: Allow participants to photograph freely while returning.
closing.assignment: Make one photograph showing how the city feels now.
closing.question: Ask them to consider whether they notice different things after completing the missions.

gallery.title: Gallery session

gather.title: Gather the shortlisted photographs
gather.body: Transfer or open only the images marked during the walk.
gather.note: Each participant should have one or two candidates from every mission.

select.title: Make final selections
select.body: Choose one image for each position in the collection.
items: Which image communicates the mission most clearly?
Where does my eye go first?
Which image makes me notice or feel something?
Which image adds something different to my collection?

sequence.title: Sequence and title
sequence.body: Participants arrange their photographs and create:
items: A one-sentence reflection beginning: “During the walk, I discovered that…”

exhibition.title: Mini exhibition
exhibition.body: Display the finished collections. Each participant introduces one photograph.
exhibition.note: Keep the final discussion celebratory and specific. Recognize observation, experimentation, persistence, and creative decisions — not only technical perfection.
items: “This photograph is called ______. I noticed ______, so I tried ______.”

gallery.reflection_stem: During the walk, I discovered that…

done.title: Session complete
done.body: The workshop is successful if participants become more curious and intentional — not if every image is technically perfect.
